why.Mount Baker Ski Area (Chair 8) traverse: Winter or spring on skis, when a party planning a ski descent starts from the ski area base and traverses down into the creek valley rather than walking the old road.

wa_mount_skokomish_standard.primary: Putvin Trail to Lake of the Angels, then west to the saddle north of Point 5945

why.Mildred Lakes Trail from Hamma Hamma Roa: When combining the climb with Mount Cruiser or Mount Lincoln, or to avoid the steep Putvin trail; the brushy off-trail stretch above the lakes is easier with lingering snow.

wa_mount_spickard_silver_glacier.primary: Depot Creek from the north side of the border, over the col between the two peaks

why.From Ross Lake by boat and up Silver Cre: To keep the whole trip inside the United States with no border crossing on foot, for parties willing to book a water taxi up Ross Lake and push through the cross-country above the cabin.

wa_mount_spickard_southwest.primary: Depot Creek from the north side of the border to the lake camp

why.From Ross Lake by boat and up Silver Cre: To keep the whole trip inside the United States with no border crossing on foot, for parties who will book a water taxi up Ross Lake and handle the long cross-country approach.

wa_mount_steel_standard.primary: Duckabush River Trail to the unmarked creek turnoff

why.First Divide and the unnamed lake basin: When the North Fork Skokomish corridor is open: it is far shorter and easier than the Duckabush walk, but fire damage has closed the trail, so check status first.

wa_mount_stone_lake_of_angels.primary: Putvin Trail from Hamma Hamma Road to Lake of the Angels

why.Lena Lake and Upper Lena Lake, the St. P: For a scenic two- or three-day trip through lake country, or to finish with a Lena Lake exit; slower and needs off-trail route-finding, so not the quick way up.

wa_mount_stuart_cascadian_couloir.primary: Longs Pass from Esmeralda TH — summer scramble

why.Longs Pass from Esmeralda TH — spring sn: Late spring, while the couloir is still filled with snow and gives a faster, steeper snow climb than the summer scree; needs axe and crampons and an early start before it softens.

wa_mount_stuart_ice_cliff_glacier.primary: Stuart Lake trailhead and the Mountaineer Creek valley to the 5,400 ft basin

why.Early-season approach with the Eightmile: Early spring, when snow or a gate closes Eightmile Road short of the trailhead and the party must add road miles on foot or skis before the usual trail.

wa_mount_stuart_north_ridge.primary: North side — Stuart Lake TH via Mountaineer Creek

why.South side — Esmeralda TH over Longs Pas: When avoiding the car shuttle: the usual Cascadian Couloir descent lands on this side, so the party walks out to its own car, at the cost of a longer, higher approach.

wa_mount_torment_south_ridge.primary: Boston Basin, rising traverse to the Taboo Glacier

why.Torment Basin climbers' path: Late season, when the moat at the top of the Taboo Glacier makes the standard line hard; steeper and brushier on the approach.

wa_mount_townsend_standard.primary: Mount Townsend Trail #839 from the Upper Trailhead

why.Little Quilcene Trail over Little River: When the small upper lot is full on a summer weekend, or for a quieter, mostly forested approach from the northeast; carry water for the dry exposed last mile.

wa_mount_washington_olympic_standard.primary: FR-2419 up the Big Creek drainage to the road-end trailhead

why.From Mount Ellinor, across the connectin: When traversing Mount Ellinor and Mount Washington in one day; a long way round if Washington is the only goal, with sustained Class 4 on the fractured ridge.
